stem: A company runs a database server on EC2 around the clock with a stable, predictable load for the next three years. It will not change instance families. Which purchasing option gives the lowest cost?
explanation: A 3-year Standard Reserved Instance gives the deepest RI discount (up to 72%) for steady, predictable usage. Convertible RIs and shorter terms discount less, and Spot Instances can be interrupted, which a database cannot tolerate.

stem: A company wants a Reserved Instance discount but expects to switch instance families and operating systems during the term. Which option should it purchase?
explanation: Convertible Reserved Instances can be exchanged for RIs with a different instance family, operating system or tenancy. Standard RIs offer a larger discount but cannot be exchanged for a different instance family.

stem: A company runs workloads on Amazon EC2, AWS Lambda and AWS Fargate and wants one flexible commitment that discounts all three. Which pricing model fits?
explanation: Compute Savings Plans apply to EC2 in any family or Region, Lambda and Fargate in exchange for a 1- or 3-year hourly spend commitment. EC2 Instance Savings Plans give a bigger discount but cover only one instance family in one Region and do not cover Lambda or Fargate.

stem: A company wants to cut Amazon EC2 costs with Spot Instances. Which workloads are good candidates? (Choose two.)
explanation: Spot Instances can be reclaimed with a two-minute warning, so they suit flexible, interruption-tolerant work such as rendering batches and stateless build workers. A long job that cannot checkpoint looks like a cheap batch job, but one interruption throws away all of its progress, and databases and checkout services need steady capacity.

stem: A company must bring existing server-bound software licenses priced per physical core and socket to AWS. Which EC2 option provides that visibility?
explanation: Dedicated Hosts give a whole physical server with visibility into sockets and cores, which bring-your-own-license terms often require. Dedicated Instances also run on single-tenant hardware but give no control over or visibility into the underlying host.

stem: A retailer needs guaranteed EC2 capacity in one Availability Zone for a two-week sales event and wants no long-term commitment. Which option should it use?
explanation: On-Demand Capacity Reservations reserve capacity in a specific Availability Zone for any duration and can be cancelled at any time. Savings Plans lower the price but do not reserve capacity, and they require a 1- or 3-year commitment.

stem: A company is estimating the hourly price of an On-Demand Amazon EC2 instance. Which factors change that price? (Choose two.)
explanation: On-Demand EC2 prices depend on the instance type and size, the Region and the operating system. The Support plan is tempting because it is also an AWS charge, but it is billed separately and does not change an instance's hourly rate.

stem: A company is estimating the network charges for a new web application. Which type of data transfer is generally free of charge?
options: Data transferred into AWS from the internet
Data transferred out of AWS to the internet
Data transferred between two AWS Regions
explanation: Inbound data transfer from the internet is generally not charged. Outbound transfer to the internet, cross-Region transfer and most cross-AZ transfer are billed per GB.

stem: A law firm must keep scanned case files for ten years. The files are almost never read, and retrieval within 12 hours is acceptable. Which S3 storage class costs least?
explanation: S3 Glacier Deep Archive has the lowest storage price, with standard retrievals completed within 12 hours. Glacier Instant Retrieval returns data in milliseconds but stores it at a higher per-GB price than needed here.

stem: An analytics team stores data with unpredictable, changing access patterns and wants storage costs optimized automatically without paying retrieval fees. Which S3 storage class should it choose?
explanation: S3 Intelligent-Tiering moves objects between access tiers based on use for a small monitoring fee and charges no retrieval fees. Standard-IA and One Zone-IA charge a per-GB retrieval fee, which adds up when access is unpredictable.

stem: An AWS Partner that resells AWS wants to group customer accounts, apply its own pricing rates and produce pro forma bills for each group. Which service should it use?
explanation: AWS Billing Conductor lets you group accounts, define custom pricing rules and generate pro forma billing data for showback or chargeback. Cost Explorer only analyzes the actual AWS charges and cannot apply custom rates.

stem: A team wants an email alert when its forecasted monthly AWS spending is expected to exceed \$5,000. Which service meets this requirement?
explanation: AWS Budgets sends alerts when actual or forecasted cost or usage exceeds a threshold you set. Cost Explorer can show forecasts but does not send alerts, and a CloudWatch billing alarm watches only actual estimated charges.

stem: A finance analyst wants to view charts of the last 12 months of spending by service and see a forecast for the coming months. Which tool should the analyst use?
explanation: AWS Cost Explorer provides an interactive view of historical costs, filtering by service, account or tag, and cost forecasts. The Cost and Usage Report is the most detailed data, but it is delivered as raw files rather than ready-made charts.

stem: Which AWS billing resource delivers the most granular, line-item cost and usage data to an Amazon S3 bucket for querying with Amazon Athena?
explanation: The AWS Cost and Usage Report, now delivered through AWS Data Exports as CUR 2.0, writes the most comprehensive line-item billing data to S3, where Athena, Redshift or QuickSight can analyze it. CloudTrail records API activity, not costs.

stem: A company planning a migration wants to estimate the monthly cost of a proposed architecture before creating any AWS resources. Which tool should it use?
explanation: AWS Pricing Calculator models the cost of services you have not deployed yet. Cost Explorer analyzes spending that has already happened, and Compute Optimizer right-sizes resources that are already running.

stem: A company with 15 AWS accounts turns on consolidated billing in AWS Organizations. Which benefits does it gain? (Choose two.)
options: One bill for all member accounts
Free Business Support for every account
Separate bills for each IAM user
explanation: Consolidated billing gives one bill for the organization and combines usage across accounts, so tiered prices and Reserved Instance or Savings Plans discounts apply more widely. It does not include a Support plan, which is still purchased and billed per account.

stem: A company wants its billing reports to break down AWS costs by department and project. What should the company do?
options: Create a separate VPC per department
explanation: After resources are tagged and the tags are activated as cost allocation tags, Cost Explorer and the Cost and Usage Report can group costs by those tags. VPCs and IAM groups organize networking and permissions, not billing data.

stem: A company wants to be notified automatically when its spending pattern suddenly deviates from normal, using machine learning to detect the change. Which service should it use?
explanation: AWS Cost Anomaly Detection uses machine learning to spot unusual spending and sends alerts with root-cause details. A CloudWatch billing alarm fires only when charges cross a fixed threshold, and Compute Optimizer gives right-sizing advice.

stem: A company needs a designated Technical Account Manager and a 15-minute response for business-critical outages, at the lowest cost. Which Support plan should it choose?
explanation: Enterprise Support assigns a designated Technical Account Manager and targets a 15-minute response for business-critical outages. Business Support+ costs less, but its fastest response target is 30 minutes and it does not include a designated TAM.

stem: A new AWS account has not purchased any Support plan. Which Support plan does it already have at no extra cost?
explanation: Basic Support comes with every AWS account and covers account and billing customer service, documentation, AWS re:Post, AWS Health and the core Trusted Advisor checks. Developer Support is tempting as the entry-level plan, but it is a paid plan.

stem: Which AWS Enterprise Support feature gives customers a team of billing and account experts for non-technical billing questions?
explanation: The Concierge Support Team, included in Enterprise Support, handles billing and account questions. The Technical Account Manager is the customer's technical advocate for architecture and operations, not billing.

stem: A finance team wants to understand what the company has already spent on AWS. Which tools provide data on past spending? (Choose two.)
explanation: Cost Explorer charts historical costs and usage, and the Cost and Usage Report (now delivered through AWS Data Exports) gives line-item detail of past charges. Pricing Calculator is tempting because it shows costs, but it estimates architectures that have not been deployed yet, and Compute Optimizer reports utilization rather than spending.

stem: A company wants to buy a third-party firewall appliance, deploy it in minutes and pay for it through its AWS bill. Which resource should it use?
explanation: AWS Marketplace is a curated catalog of third-party software that can be deployed quickly and billed through the AWS account. The Partner Network is a program for consulting and technology partners, not a software storefront.

stem: A company notices that an Amazon EC2 instance in another AWS account is sending spam and port scans to its servers. Whom should the company report this to?
explanation: The AWS Abuse team (AWS Trust & Safety) investigates reports of AWS resources used for spam, port scanning, DDoS or other abuse. AWS Health Dashboard shows service events affecting your own account and does not take abuse reports.
